`a_c` makes no claim of universal applicability, logical completeness,
consistency, decidability, soundness, or category-theoretic status except where
an exact, separately identified proof establishes that claim for a declared
fragment, model, or relation.

Given explicit interpretation and typed subject, resolved compatible references on one exact basis are required before consuming a model judgment. The standard owns its additional signature, record, closure and classification choices; finite capacity and predecessor provenance do not uniquely derive them. AC-007/014 consume shared results; AC-016 consumes conjunction for claims requiring several judgments. The transformation library provides reusable responsibilities without replacing AC-013 or establishing categorical functor laws. Universal applicability, completeness, consistency, decidability, soundness and categorical status are not asserted absent the specified proof exception.

grounding.quote:
This standard introduces the generic calculus identities `F_D`, `F_P`, and
`F_H`. It does not import those identities from an equal-spelled graph,
runtime, ODD, or application shorthand. The predecessor clauses motivated the
substrate-neutral evaluation, probabilistic-processing, human-adjudication,
authority, evidence, and refusal distinctions. This member selects the three
generic kinds below; their inventory is a calculus policy, not a theorem forced
by those predecessor clauses. Nominal equality with a predecessor or downstream shorthand
creates no concept-identity, import, or equivalence relation.

Interpretation requires no implicit STDO representation, GTL carrier or downstream implementation. F_D/F_P/F_H are chosen generic calculus identities, not imports or equivalents of same-spelled graph, runtime, ODD or application shorthands. Basis issuance resolves relative provenance links to absolute predecessor-cut semantic addresses in derivation_basis.principle_refs within derivation_basis.release_uri; mutable authoring links are not digest-bound references. exceptions: A population may be empty only if the selected signature does not require a member of that kind.
Another fundamental family requires an explicit compatible calculus extension, not an extra subject sort.

grounding.quote:
`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population is
finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and record
identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be that union.
Then `I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M`, where every member of
`External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared external reference
domain and exact resolution relation. A hidden record, an unpopulated extra
record family, an identity occurring in two populations, or an identity in `I`
with neither one local record nor one lawful external resolution refuses the
model. A population may be empty only when the selected signature does not
require a member of that record kind.

predicate.statement: Every signature imports the eight core identities unchanged; specialization can constrain fields, values, references and admissible kinds, but cannot remove, rename, shadow or silently add core families. Unknown fields/kinds require a new signature or explicit compatible extension. Population_M is total, finite and disjoint with globally unique record identities. Hidden records, extra unpopulated families, duplicate population membership or identities lacking exactly one lawful local/external resolution refuse the model. Every identity-bearing scalar or collection member is checked through RefDomain_Sigma; local targets satisfy the exact family and, for semantic objects, sort, while external targets satisfy exactly one declared kind and basis relation. Local/external dual resolution, missing domains, wrong families/sorts, ambiguity and dangling external identities refuse structural admission.

grounding.quote:
The following sections define the exact shapes of the eight core record
families. `SemanticObject`, `TypedRelation`, `Constraint`, `Latitude`, and
`Residual` populate `O`, `E`, `C`, `L`, and `X`. The traversal,
transformation, and judgment records defined below populate `V`, `T`, and `J`.
A traversal, transformation, or judgment is not placed in `O` merely by
reifying its name as a semantic object. A subject model may independently
represent the concept of a record kind, but that representation does not
satisfy the core population law.

A traversal, transformation or judgment cannot satisfy its core population obligation by reifying its name in O. grounding.quote:
These arguments apply [F1–F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments)
to a governed symbolic model under a declared signature and interpretation.
The model's records represent a separately identified subject; some predicates
admit mechanical decision and others require semantic judgment. These are the

grounding.quote:
| the exact predicate is established under its governing latitude | `satisfied` |
| an admissible counterexample defeats that predicate | `falsified` |
| evidence cannot decide that predicate, including a missing required reason | `indeterminate` |
| deciding the predicate needs material scope or capability outside the evaluation contract | `out_of_frame` |
| its subject or governing basis cannot support interpretation of the predicate | `invalid_basis` |

predicate.statement: Each constraint binds applies_to, predicate, basis, judgment_kind, latitude_ref and refusal to Evaluate. The exact predicate on applies_to is the claim. Established predicate under governing latitude maps to satisfied; an admissible counterexample to falsified; undecidable evidence or missing required reason to indeterminate; required material scope/capability outside contract to out_of_frame; uninterpretable subject/governing basis to invalid_basis. Core diagnosis and missing-reason rules retain independent counterevidence; multiple required predicates use core conjunction, not arbitrary row selection. Foundations owns verdicts, legal performance pairs, effects and missing-reason handling, carried by AC-014.

grounding.quote:
`hold`, `gap`, `refusal` and `refuse` always carry a declared cause: an undecided
predicate maps to `indeterminate`; missing material frame scope or capability
to `out_of_frame`; an unusable basis to `invalid_basis`; and an admissible
counterexample to that predicate to `falsified`. An established prohibition
falsifies only the permission or admission predicate it defeats. Refusing an
interpreter because its grant is absent does not falsify the model's constraint
predicate. On that constraint, retain the actual evaluation performance and
any separately admissible counterevidence or supported scope/basis diagnosis;
without deciding support the unevaluated predicate remains `indeterminate`.
The refusal of permission is a separately bound result.

predicate.statement: Returned projections, successors and candidates satisfy only an established declared production predicate; absent output defeats that predicate only with contract/evidence support. Accepted/admitted mean a decision over an exact unchanged subject, mandate and bound authority: lawful supported decision is satisfied, established decision-contract violation falsified, undecided decision/grant indeterminate; scope/capability and basis diagnoses attach to the evaluation lacking them. Hold/gap/refusal/refuse require declared causes with the same reason-sensitive mappings. A prohibition defeats only its permission/admission predicate. Missing interpreter grant does not falsify a model constraint: preserve actual performance, admissible counterevidence and supported diagnoses; without deciding support the unevaluated constraint remains indeterminate. Original outcome plus cause defines the refinement; a bare stop word cannot satisfy a consumer. Implementations bind mappings before execution and retain performance, known effects, evidence and residuals. No outcome establishes another model's truth or upgrades actual performance/effects.

grounding.quote:
Projection, compression, interpretation, or encoding cannot erase a residual.
It remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent authority, or
causes refusal.

Every material uncertainty, omission, translation loss, unresolved boundary,
or unproven relation remains in `X` until an authorized disposition creates an
exact successor model. Absence from a projection is not resolution.

judgment probes to resolve material uncertainty. Use unit evidence for
module-owned laws under the testing frames. Schedule substantial,
resource-intensive user-acceptance cycles near release or when a bounded
capability is considered complete enough to qualify. An early focused user
probe remains appropriate when it decides a material outcome uncertainty.

predicate.statement: Establish the smallest runnable thread early; extend/revalidate existing affected threads and expand bounded increments by consequential uncertainty, dependency/interface reach and failure impact. Early E2E/integration evidence constrains incompatible choices, settles exercised interfaces and preserves working composition while focusing unresolved obligations. Passing threads establish only exercised relations/conditions; untested branches, combinations, refusals and recovery keep proof obligations. Revisit settled choices when material counterevidence invalidates basis. Use focused deterministic regression, targeted judgment probes and module-law unit evidence during construction; substantial resource-intensive UAT belongs near release or sufficient bounded-capability completion. Distinct testing claims still govern scenarios, independence and repetitions; reuse requires supported applicability, affected reassessment and mandatory gates.

Return a required repair outside that territory to its owner; understanding the

retained guards and acceptance predicates as well as new findings. An excluded
threat alone gives no retention claim; a proposed wider threat model re-enters
its owner. Internal location alone does not establish trust, and hypothetical
hostility alone does not establish applicability. Retain the actual untrusted
input, mutable-state, authority and effect checks required by the supported
model. A suggested repair becomes an obligation only through its proper owner.

Techniques that serve this, none of them mandatory and none of them exhaustive:

- **cross-context invariance**: separate what holds wherever the entity appears
  from what a particular context adds, where multiple contexts exist
- **null-peer comparison**: name a structurally similar entity the operating
  model treats differently, and state what separates them
- **adjoint round-trip**: interpret the entity through an adjacent domain's
  treatment surface and back through its adjoint mapping, and show the identity
  claim survives
- **transplant**: show what a neighbouring entity would have to acquire to be
  treated as this one
- **coat stripping**: vary or remove contextual claims and show identity
  survives; vary an identity claim and show it does not

grounding.quote: # The STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems

The **STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems**, written `a_c`,

Its how bindings locate authoritative HOW, with build_tenants/ as the default software-development location; it carries design, GTL publications, code, tests and local proof surfaces.

grounding.quote:
The Product Definition Overlay's `what` bindings locate the authoritative `WHAT`.
`specification/` is the default software-development location.

The Product Definition Overlay's `how` bindings locate the authoritative `HOW`.
`build_tenants/` is the default software-development location.

value.label: Product Specification and Product Realization

value.definition: ODD service/query layers can provide transport, sessions, routing, browser-safe projections and API surfaces. Visible current state projects admitted runtime facts and constructive history, not the whole material workspace; the workspace remains current construction reality.

grounding.quote:
Service or query layers may own:

- transport
- sessions
- routing
- browser-safe projection
- API surfaces

This projection describes admitted runtime facts, not the whole material
workspace. The workspace remains the current reality being constructed. Fresh
observation can expose divergence from an earlier projection or belief;
admission then records the relevant evidence under the existing authority.

value.label: ODD projections and service layers

conditions: Applies to every ODD product over GTL/ABG.
value.definition: The method-level homeostasis loop runs from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation to next lawful action. Its four distinct functions are synthesize_model, eval_gap, evaluate_next and evaluate_action.

grounding.quote:
Every ODD product over GTL/ABG must preserve one constructive evaluation loop
from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation to next lawful
action.

value.label: Constructive evaluation and yield loop

value.definition: The selected Product outcome under STDO-UP-013 is external authority for material work. An admitted bounded prerequisite or experiment supplies a bounded work basis without permitting the loop to author, select or enlarge the outcome.

grounding.quote:
The selected Product outcome under `STDO-UP-013` is external authority for this
loop. Product models, gaps, assurance, ledgers, and projections may interpret
that outcome but cannot author, select, or enlarge it.

value.label: Selected Product outcome and bounded basis

value.definition: Loop carrier vocabulary: IntentLineage is admitted human, imported-source, prior-product, intent-engine or prior-construction intent with ABG event-log lineage; ProductAssetModel is desired and known typed assets synthesized from lineage, prior model and admitted product truth, with admitted publication basis, not runtime fact or action authority. Worksite is workspace, runtime archive, transform assets, product asset root, profile and observed file/process state, not authority itself. RuntimeEventLog is append-only admitted runtime facts; RuntimeProjection is replay-derived state over that log and execution basis. ObservationSnapshot is a read-only runtime/worksite view carried by ABG with product rows. GapPressureRow represents missing, partial, blocked, waiting or ambiguous asset/evidence pressure. ActionCatalog publishes lawful graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs and eligible outcomes. PriorityProjection deterministically ranks bound lawful actions under visible policy. ConstructionIntent is an admitted action for one bounded invocation preserving outcome/bounded-basis references. AdmittedEvidence covers worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness and postflight evidence; it is not worker self-closure. NextActionProjection reads NextActionBasis and current truth and selects only lawful graph action.

grounding.quote: | `RuntimeEventLog` | Append-only admitted runtime facts. | ABG runtime truth. |

value.label: Typed loop carriers

value.definition: TargetObligationBinding binds gap pressure to the exact selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence references and admissible graph outcomes. It is a product-domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority.

grounding.quote: | `TargetObligationBinding` | Exact binding from gap pressure to the selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence refs, and admissible graph outcomes. | Product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. |

value.label: TargetObligationBinding

value.definition: NextActionBasis is dispatch data, not another controller: initial_selection or an explicit post-action basis derived from EdgeClosureDecision: post_yield_resume, post_close_graph_continuation, post_retry, post_repair, post_reenter, post_reprice or post_block. post_reprice records a re-entry request without action-selection authority.

grounding.quote: `post_reprice` records a re-entry request and carries no action-selection authority.

value.label: NextActionBasis

value.definition: synthesize_model consumes IntentLineage, prior ProductAssetModel and admitted product truth and returns ProductAssetModel. It may update desired and known typed asset truth; it may not observe the worksite, admit construction intent, select, invoke or close work.

grounding.quote: Model synthesis. It may update desired and known typed asset truth. It must not observe the worksite, admit construction intent, select work, invoke work, or close work.

value.label: synthesize_model

value.definition: eval_gap consumes ProductAssetModel, RuntimeEventLog, RuntimeProjection and Worksite and returns ObservationSnapshot and GapPressureRow. It read-only compares desired truth to observed reality, emitting pressure only; it may not admit construction intent or choose, invoke or close work.

grounding.quote: Read-only gap discovery. It compares desired model truth to observed reality and emits missing, partial, blocked, waiting, or ambiguous asset pressure.

value.label: eval_gap

value.definition: evaluate_next consumes NextActionBasis, fresh eval_gap truth, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog and Policy; returns PriorityProjection, NextActionProjection and selected_action, or the applicable typed no-action. It binds obligations and ranks lawful published actions, without admitting construction intent or classifying the prior action; prior-action classification comes from the admitted EdgeClosureDecision.
exceptions: Unresolved post_reprice returns typed no-action pending separately admitted constitutional authority.

grounding.quote: It may bind target obligations and rank lawful actions, but does not admit construction intent or decide whether the prior action closed, yielded, failed or requires repair; it consumes the admitted EdgeClosureDecision for that classification.

value.label: evaluate_next

value.definition: evaluate_action consumes ConstructionIntent, AdmittedEvidence, TargetObligationBinding and Policy; returns EdgeFulfillmentLedger and EdgeClosureDecision for the action just taken. It evaluates close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice or block; it may not admit construction intent, invoke work or choose the next graph action.

grounding.quote: Action-result evaluation only. It decides close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice, or block for the action just taken.

value.label: evaluate_action

value.definition: The governed work pair comprises mutable workspace W and immutable ledger L of closure-relevant admitted work; immutable event log E orders and anchors entries with predecessor references. Evaluator work Ev evaluates a declared L snapshot. L records callout basis, observed deltas, file references, digests, execution evidence, touched obligations, claims, evaluator inputs/outputs and admission status, rather than copying W. EdgeFulfillmentLedger is the evidence/convergence carrier for an edge attempt or version, including counts, obligation rows, materialization/liveness/admission references and edge_converged.

grounding.quote:
The ledger is not
a copy of the workspace; it is the admitted trace of callout basis, observed
deltas, file refs, digests, execution evidence, obligations touched, claims
made, evaluator inputs, evaluator outputs, and admission status.

value.label: Workspace, ledger and event spine

value.definition: EdgeClosureDecision is the replay-visible sum type close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice or block. These domain dispositions refine the shared result algebra; each has basis/reason references and an explicit predicate about lawful issuance. Yield retains the same lawful edge/attempt, admitted progress or waiting state and replay-visible resume basis, adding no failure classification; it is distinct from retry, block, timeout and local CLI looping.

grounding.quote:
A lawful decision
can be `satisfied` while the edge's fitness remains falsified or unresolved.

same edge or attempt remains lawful
progress or waiting state is admitted
resume basis is replay-visible
the yield disposition adds no failure classification; retained assessments remain

value.label: EdgeClosureDecision and yield

value.definition: ODD is the graph-native product-authoring method for GTL/ABG domain products. It requires typed assets, named graph functions, published catalog, operative GTL module, ABG execution authority, one constructive loop, projections over constructive history and lawful manual explainability. Framework realization proceeds outcome traversals first, declarative GTL/ABG structure second, minimal imperative adapters last.

grounding.quote: Operative framework behavior must be built outcome-first: outcome traversals first, declarative GTL/ABG carrier structure second, and minimal imperative adapter code last.

value.label: ODD Method

value.definition: Manual walkthrough is the explanatory traversal using only declared authority: identify current typed asset/node; next lawful vector and published graph-function carrier; required inputs, evaluators, output contract and carried environment; construct/assess the next asset or checkpoint; repeat to target-relative closure. A vector is a constitutional transition contract and a graph function its published constructive realization.

grounding.quote: A human operator, using only the declared authority surfaces, should be able to:

value.label: Manual walkthrough

value.definition: Agentic conformance has an F_P walkthrough proving process followability and an F_D artifact-admission gate. The real-work walkthrough covers intake triage, smallest lawful re-entry, spec/requirement/design/ticket chain, constructive evaluation and closure proof using declared authority. A minimal packet carries input/output contract, required context, role, evaluator regime, provenance and the smallest sufficient authority with source references; compression is prompt input, never deciding authority.

grounding.quote: Conformance has two halves: an F_P proof that the process is followable, and an F_D gate that admits the produced artifacts.

value.label: Conforming agentic development

conditions: For an ODD or graph-native boundary.
value.definition: Closure-grade negative proof exercises the supported Product authority path with the real authority-bearing input invalidated, identifies entry and governing authority, proves refusal before prohibited effect and proves no legacy, fallback, reconstruction or parallel path succeeds. Source, packaged, installed and runtime absence are separate claims. Where applicable the path is public entry → admitted GTL topology → named GraphFunction work contract → implementation/plugin admitted seam → ABG traversal/event/continuation/replay truth → replay-derived projection → typed Product outcome or continuation.

grounding.quote:
Closure-grade negative evidence identifies the supported entry and governing
authority, invalidates the real authority-bearing input, exercises the
supported path, proves refusal before the prohibited effect, and establishes
that no legacy, fallback, reconstruction, or parallel path succeeds. Source,
packaged, installed, and runtime absence are distinct claims.

value.label: Real authority-path negative proof

value.definition: Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces, beyond test documentation. Declared scenarios and use cases are described as the best proving-path source because they pressure feature intent and design decisions and guide significant code/control path selection.

grounding.quote:
Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces.

They are not only test documentation.

value.label: Scenario bundle

value.definition: Release version belongs to release process/metadata rather than constitutional graph truth. Immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement and exact-cut acceptance are a separate process surface; graph-native method concerns current assets, vectors, closures and authority.

grounding.quote:
Immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement, and exact-cut
acceptance remain a separate process surface.

value.label: ODD release boundary

value.definition: Source-bound failure families route decisions to owners rather than create another checklist: missing graph structure/carriers → Graph Model, Typed Assets, Graph Functions, Outcome-First Realization and GTL Module; imperative-first or hidden continuation → Outcome-First, ABG Continuation, Execution Authority Audit and A0/four functions; unexplained traversal or ungated artifacts → Manual Walkthrough and Agentic Development; builder/private-target coupling or self-host authority merger → Product/Self-Host boundaries and Installed-Dev; inadequate scenarios or unevidenced closure → Scenario Rule, A6 and negative proof; last-output composition or zoom disagreement → Cumulative Environment, Global Convergence and A14; flattened yield → A4/A8/A9/A10; query/postflight/service/operator selection → Projection-Source Coherence and A4a/A7/A11/A12/A16.

grounding.quote:
Use the following source-bound failure families; they select
deciding owners rather than define another checklist law.

value.label: ODD conformance failure families

conditions: An agent or designer is instructed to build a product using ODD_METHOD.
value.definition: The expected sequence is: read SPEC_METHOD and preserve its chain; read any product-specific method; read local INTENT, PRODUCT, requirements and designs; identify source-to-outcome semantics, typed assets and public graph carriers; define machine-readable catalog and GTL outer/live boundaries; define coarse/refined/proof closure coherence; audit affected runtime/plugin/worker/event/projection/assurance/closure/continuation authority; define the full constructive loop; define dispositions including lawful yield; define query/projection history and source coherence; only then implement code, policy and transport. Imperative-first scripts, documentation-only graph wrappers and hidden service carriers are excluded.

grounding.quote: 14. only then implement code, policy, and transport surfaces

value.label: ODD invocation sequence

conditions: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product.
value.definition: Cold-start acquisition follows a product-specific ordered route.

grounding.quote: When starting cold in a concrete ODD product, use this order.

value.label: Cold-start reading order

value.definition: Posts are repository commentary for analysis, criticism, proposed changes, handoff and repricing confidence. They convey observations/proposals through shared transformations, may influence specification/design, and do not themselves supply constitutional truth or adoption decisions.

grounding.quote: Posts are not constitutional truth. They are working commentary that may later influence specification or design.

value.label: Post

value.definition: The post carrier is bound by the Product Definition Overlay's ticketing.comments.root. Its default local-file location is .ai-workspace/comments/<agent>/; .ai-workspace/comments/<agent-id>/ is a capability example.

grounding.quote:
Posts live at the Product Definition Overlay's `ticketing.comments.root`
binding.

value.label: Bound commentary carrier

value.definition: Post categories are REVIEW: critique of code/spec/design/post; STRATEGY: proposed technical or methodological direction; GAP: precise insufficiency or contradiction; SCHEMA: data/event/interface/contract shape; HANDOFF: bounded context/task-state transfer; MATRIX: explicit comparison of decision options.

grounding.quote:
- `REVIEW` for critique of code, spec, design, or another post
- `STRATEGY` for a proposed technical or methodological direction
- `GAP` for a precise insufficiency or contradiction
- `SCHEMA` for data model, event model, interface, or contract shape
- `HANDOFF` for bounded transfer of context or task state
- `MATRIX` for explicit decision comparison across options

value.label: Post categories

value.definition: The post base template has heading CATEGORY: Subject; Author; ISO-8601 Date; Addresses identifying the artifact, issue or boundary; Status initially Draft; optional ISO-8601 Updated; Summary, Analysis and Recommended Action sections. MATRIX uses a central decision table instead of free prose.
value.label: Post template

value.definition: Reusable method change preserves authority causality: incident/review evidence → shared-method intake → one owning standard → consistency and independent review → human-authority acceptance → one complete released STDO version → explicit consumer selection → consumer-owned realization and evidence. This describes authority causality, not a prescribed intake workflow or artifact set.

grounding.quote: This is authority causality, not a prescribed intake workflow or artifact set.

value.label: Shared method adoption and propagation

value.definition: The Standards Library includes deciding methods, foundational contracts and non-deciding views. A complete cut also includes declared projections, schemas, templates, frames and interaction assets. A selectable release is one complete immutable constitutional member set with exact identity, manifest and membership. Source-line Product Definition identity and immutable Product/release identities retain distinct source-owned relations; subordinate executable/interaction tooling retains separate responsibilities.

grounding.quote:
A selectable
release has one complete immutable constitutional member set with exact cut
identity, manifest and membership.

value.label: Standards Library

value.definition: The README attributes finite capacity, interpretation, purpose, identity, typed composition, total handling, judgment/authority separation, result algebra/conjunction, workspace context and configuration to Foundations. It attributes contract application, constraint surfaces, faithful projection and composition to Transformation Library. Bind, Acquire, Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose organize these responsibilities. These are named external owner roles, not imported implementations.

grounding.quote:
Bind, Acquire,
Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose organise these responsibilities. Domain
instances bind their predicates, policies and grants; they do not copy a rival
generic law or acquire a new runtime API.

value.label: Foundations and shared library owner roles

value.definition: Task routes: intake/re-entry → Spec intake/classification and Ticket carrier selection when admitting work, with Triage/carrier excerpts; recovery → Foundations workspace/context then library work/recovery; evidence reuse → Foundations change-impact and library contract/currentness; outcome fitness → Foundations bounded construction, assertions/observations and assurance provenance; results → Foundations algebra/conjunction plus applicable domain refinement; candidate assessment/disposition → Spec construction/assessment/delegation and proportional disposition plus Foundations authority. Evaluation/conjunction frames collect the three evidence/fitness/result routes. Constitutional-derivation projects library, Design and enclosing Spec admission; domain-binding covers continuation/projection/Markov overlays; release/adoption covers publication/qualification/conservation/adoption; member construction/assessment supplies generic member rules, still requiring actual Product requirements and acceptance criteria.

grounding.quote:
Start with the owner sections for the actual question. Bind their material
inputs to the selected Product, subject, outcome, evidence and existing grant.

value.label: Task owner routes and excerpt assemblies

value.definition: The README maps formal calculus to Axiomatic Calculus; generic frame law to Reference Frame Method and bounded-context term resolution to Spec; actor/Executive configurations to Baseline; constitutional WHAT/construction to Spec; structural HOW/transformation admission/realization to Design Module; names/identities to Identity; graph-native domain to ODD; optional application-neutral traversal model to Traversal Occurrence Profile; state/treatment/world-model claims to World Model; UX to UX Method; work carriers to Ticket; cuts/conservation/publication/adoption protocol to Release, Product-definition routing to Spec and adoption decisions to consumers; commentary/writing to Posting/Writing Guides; semantic discovery/locator resolution to Glossary. These are owner locators, not substitute owner definitions.

grounding.quote:
The Glossary
owns resolution of its locators, while each located method owns its meaning.

value.label: Method owner catalog

value.definition: Distribution surfaces include digest-bound non-deciding compressions, starter templates for Product Definition/specification/project frames/agent bootstrap, normative layout-neutral Product Definition Overlay and deterministic installed-release manifest schemas, and interaction assets that route work without minting authority or a workflow engine. Symbolic method interpretation supplies encoded determinations, source routes and unresolved conditions; its document inventory differs from package inventory.

grounding.quote:
Plugin interaction assets route work;
they mint no authority or workflow engine.

value.label: Distribution and entry surfaces

value.definition: Named source member Reference Frame Method.

grounding.quote: # Reference Frame Method

value.label: Reference Frame Method

value.definition: Reference-frame engagement responds to finite actor context, attention, time and capability. An activated frame combines declared evaluation family, exact workspace/topology basis, finite material relations/coordinates, invariants/authorities, evidence/exclusions and actor envelope; outcomes use satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame or invalid_basis. Project engagement combines workspace/outcome, practice/failures, capabilities and human judgment into frame sets, bounded evaluations, needed conjunction/translation, coverage/residuals and empirical revision. Selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision remain separate. Atomic engagement means one bounded evaluable context, not semantic irreducibility or merged authority.

grounding.quote:
`Atomic engagement unit` names the unit that can be activated and evaluated as
one bounded context. It does not assert that every relation inside the frame is
one irreducible semantic atom. A frame may carry several semantic atoms and
several owner relations without merging their meaning or authority.

value.label: Bounded frame engagement

value.definition: An evaluation is a declared question with known predicate, admissible evidence, decision authority and, where it performs material action, operation authority. It can seek judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation, using the core result algebra or declared reason-sensitive RF-012 refinement. An evaluation family groups questions requiring the same material manifold, authority basis and result binding/refinement; similar wording does not establish membership.

grounding.quote:
An evaluation family groups questions that require the same material relation
manifold, authority basis, and result binding or refinement of that one algebra.
Similar wording does not prove that two evaluations belong to the same family.

value.label: Evaluation and evaluation family

value.definition: Workspace is the bounded material body reasoned over or acted upon: potentially sources, domain assets, designs, implementations, tools, runtime, evidence, history, external dependencies and human decisions. It exceeds a repository, which is one carrier; material state differs from the acquired view. Observed state can defeat a stale summary, which cannot change state; external effects require observations from their owners.

grounding.quote:
Observed state can defeat a stale summary; the summary cannot change the state.
External effects require observations from their owning surfaces.

value.label: Workspace

value.definition: Basis identifies the exact evaluation state and every version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change could alter the evaluation. It may be immutable or moving; moving bases must declare advancement detection and reevaluation conditions.

grounding.quote:
A basis may be immutable or moving. A moving basis must declare how advancement
is detected and when reevaluation is required.

value.label: Basis

value.definition: A relation is material to an evaluation if a lawful change can change its result, invalidate its basis, change admissible evidence, operation authority or decision authority. Materiality is evaluation-relative; a relation can be material in one frame and irrelevant in another.

grounding.quote:
Materiality is evaluation-relative. A relation may be material in one frame and
irrelevant in another.

value.label: Material relation

value.definition: A material-relation manifold is the finite, jointly interpretable set of variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions needed by an evaluation family. The term denotes bounded relation space with possibly overlapping coordinate charts, without requiring geometric mathematics or runtime abstraction.

grounding.quote:
`Manifold` names a bounded relation space with potentially overlapping
coordinate charts. It does not require geometric mathematics or a runtime
manifold abstraction.

value.label: Material-relation manifold

value.definition: A coordinate is the complete local interpretive position of a value, event, decision, observation or action, including required basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority. Equality requires a declared relation; matching names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions is insufficient.

grounding.quote:
Equal names, values, shapes, locations, or apparent topology positions do not
establish coordinate equality. Equality follows a declared relation.

value.label: Coordinate

value.definition: Topology is the material entity, capability, authority, lifecycle, adjacency and seam relation structure visible to a frame at one basis, not necessarily the entire workspace topology. A state-value change preserves topology only if every such material entity/relation/lifecycle/authority/capability/adjacency/seam is preserved; changing any is topology mutation and may invalidate coordinates.

grounding.quote:
A state-value change preserves the frame topology only when it preserves every
material entity, relation, lifecycle, authority, capability, adjacency, and
seam.

value.label: Topology

value.definition: Evidence is the exact observation/artifact admitted for evaluation, carrying provenance, subject identity, basis and scope. Availability within a frame does not make it semantic truth or decision authority. Reliance binds Construction assurance to predicate, observations and consuming decision: assertion provenance supports the expected predicate; execution provenance identifies acquired subject/result. Small frames or authenticated observations alone do not establish sound, complete decisions.

grounding.quote:
Evidence does
not become semantic truth or decision authority merely because it is available
inside a frame.

value.label: Frame evidence

value.definition: Authority vocabulary distinguishes human frame-set declaration/acceptance authority; semantic meaning owner; evaluation-permitted role; owner-issued operation grant for construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation; decision role for acceptance/rejection/disposition; and actual human/agent/tool/process identity. Read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; effectful evaluation names its existing grant. Human authority can act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy where governing law permits; their identities remain distinct.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded
proxy where the governing identity and authority law permits it. Proxy identity
and human-authority identity remain distinct.

value.label: Frame authority distinctions

value.definition: Frame disjointness is structural absence of shared material variables, coordinates, evidence or result dependency for declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is procedural non-consumption/non-influence of another's unclosed working results despite possible shared subject/manifold and later conjunction of closed results. Assurance independence is claim-relative separation required by its governing law: non-authorship, evidence acquisition, reference exposure, actors and configuration. None follows from another or from the unqualified word independent.

grounding.quote:
Disjoint frames need not be independently evaluated, and independently
activated evaluations need not be disjoint. The unqualified word
`independent` does not establish any of these relations by itself.

value.label: Disjointness and independence

value.definition: Capability envelope declares competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable evaluation/assurance independence and configuration needed for activation/evaluation. Usability can differ by actor; capability can justify frame size or activation sequence changes, never invariant waiver or authority expansion.

grounding.quote:
Actor
capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence. It cannot
waive an invariant or widen authority.

value.label: Capability envelope

value.definition: A reference frame is a finite evaluation contract for one declared family over a stated basis. Its optional formal description F=<Q,B,M,C,I,A,E,X,R,J,K,D> denotes evaluation family; workspace/topology basis; material manifold; coordinate/equality law; invariants; authority; evidence/provenance; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; shared result algebra and refinements; invalidation/rechart conditions; capability; optional inter-frame dependencies/overlaps/inputs/outputs. This is a relation specification, not a required schema/runtime. Binding resolves every material coordinate to exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition. Source-linked prose can express it; representation cannot create, widen or replace binding. Prompts, packets and symbolic programs project activated frames rather than being the frame itself.

grounding.quote:
The binding may be expressed entirely in source-linked prose; representation
cannot create, widen, or replace it.

value.label: Reference frame

value.definition: An activated frame binds a declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary. A reusable declaration is not evidence of correct particular activation.

grounding.quote:
An **activated frame** binds one frame declaration to an exact evaluation,
workspace subject, basis, actor, and evidence acquisition boundary. A reusable
frame declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct.

value.label: Activated frame

value.definition: A frame set is a human-declared family available for governed outcome/workspace, potentially including overlaps, alternatives, specialists, broad exploration and separately activated assurance. It need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology.

grounding.quote:
A frame set is not required to be a partition, tree, stack, or exhaustive
ontology.

value.label: Frame set

value.definition: An active frame configuration contains frame activations and declared result relations for one evaluation/decision: one or several disjoint, overlapping or composed frames. Separate activations may overlap or be disjoint.

grounding.quote:
An **active frame configuration** is the set of frame activations and declared
result relations used for one evaluation or decision.

value.label: Active frame configuration

value.definition: A lens is a reusable question family across a frame configuration, such as authority, capability/reuse, temporal behavior, transport or proof. It becomes a frame only after instantiation with bounded evaluation, basis, manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and capability envelope.

grounding.quote:
A lens becomes a frame only when it is instantiated with a bounded evaluation,
basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra, and capability
envelope.

value.label: Lens

value.definition: Role allocates responsibility/authority; persona changes approach/salience; abstraction hides/contracts detail; component is a structural subject part. Each can assist frame construction/activation, but none is a frame by identity. Components and frames can cross each other's boundaries many-to-many.

grounding.quote:
Each may help construct or activate a frame. None is a reference frame by
identity alone. One component may appear in several frames, and one frame may
cross several components.

value.label: Role, persona, abstraction and component

value.definition: Method-function signatures describe relations rather than required APIs: declare(human authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities)→frame set; activate(frame,evaluation,subject,basis,actor)→activation or refusal; evaluate(activation,evidence)→result+evidence+residuals; conjoin(rule,results)→core result+conflicts+residuals; translate(source frame,target frame,value/evidence,mapping)→translated value, declared loss or refusal; audit_coverage(workspace,outcome,inventory,set)→ledger; revise(set,new evidence,failures,capability/topology change)→proposed delta. Returned domain outputs use RF-012 for each evaluated claim; authorized Dispose is separate from conjunction, and finer mapping is bound before consumption.

grounding.quote:
A returned `decision` does not prove it is authorised or
correct without that judgment. The frame binds any
finer case mapping before its outcome is consumed.

value.label: Frame method functions

value.definition: Joint frame participation has four distinct relations: independently activated co-evaluation, result conjunction, evidence/coordinate translation and material composition.

grounding.quote: Frames participate together through four distinct relations.

value.label: Joint frame participation

value.definition: Frame relation vocabulary: disjoint means no shared material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency; overlapping means some shared variables/evidence/entities; complementary means distinct evaluations inform one decision; alternative means evaluating the same claim under declared capability/evidence conditions; refinement resolves an aggregated distinction; restriction evaluates a lawful domain subset; translation moves values/evidence by declared coordinate map; temporal succession evaluates changed basis; composition forms one governed evaluation/action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where a real authority/decomposition relation exists. No relation is universal default; only needed evaluation/coverage relations are declared.

grounding.quote:
No one relation is the default universal frame topology. A project declares
only the relations needed for its evaluations and coverage claims.

value.label: Frame relation vocabulary

value.definition: Coverage(W,G,B,E,S,T) binds workspace, governed outcome, exact basis, known evaluation inventory, declared frame set and claim time/immutable checkpoint. Changing any material member may invalidate the coverage result.

grounding.quote: Changing any material member may invalidate the coverage result.

value.label: Coverage basis

value.definition: The known evaluation inventory records provenance and materiality from every material available source, including applicable goals/intent/Product/requirements/method; design/Ontology/identities/lifecycles/authorities/algorithms; implementation/external behavior; operational/release/security/safety/governance obligations; dependencies/seams; evidence/tests/scenarios/qualification/acceptance; tickets/check-ins/commentary/postmortems/incidents/rejections; long loops/resets/repairs/rival paths; actor limitations/invisible violations; external law/contracts/standards. Presence, counts and repository reachability do not prove coverage.

grounding.quote:
The inventory records provenance and materiality. Artifact presence, file
count, operation count, test count, or repository reachability does not prove
evaluation coverage.

value.label: Evaluation inventory

governed Product scope or outcome. It binds:
