value.definition: Execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable frame declaration or active configuration, exact evaluation, subject, basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope; distinct from the durable collective basis.

grounding.quote:
An **Agent Frame Activation**
is the execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable
frame declaration or active configuration, exact evaluation, subject, basis,
evidence boundary, and capability envelope.

value.label: Agent Frame Activation

value.definition: The SPEC_METHOD-owned build-tenancy context, urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy, relates one constitutional requirements WHAT to one or more independent project-owned HOW realizations. A tenant is one realization; multiple independent realizations constitute multi-build-tenancy. WHAT specifies admissible states, outcomes, constraints, evidence and permitted changes. Tenant design binds operations, composition, actors or mechanisms, effects, assumptions and observations through software, hardware, people, organisations or mixtures.

grounding.quote:
A
**build tenant** is one such realization. **Build tenancy** is the one-or-more
relation; one tenant is its singleton case and multi-build-tenancy begins when
the same `WHAT` has more than one independent realization.

value.label: Build tenancy, WHAT and HOW

value.definition: Canonical locators distinguish constitutional WHAT, tenant realizations and work carriers: what.intent and what.product each have one canonical entrypoint; what.specification may name multiple surfaces. how.build_tenants is the Tenant Registry; how.common binds an explicitly shared realization law. ticketing.goals, tickets, comments and optional sprints locate work-wave, ticket, commentary and execution-batch surfaces.

grounding.quote:
The **Tenant Registry** is the canonical `how.build_tenants` collection for the
product's independent `HOW` realizations. Each entry has stable identity and
locates its root, design, and implementation surfaces. The **Common Build-Tenant Surface**
is the realization law bound by `how.common` and
explicitly adopted across more than one tenant.

value.label: Definition and work carriers

value.definition: Recursive discovery of stdo_*.json throughout a selected workspace, including root and arbitrarily deep project roots; explicit directed composition relates otherwise independent definitions through target locator, stable target identity, relation authority and non-empty governing contract references.

grounding.quote:
Directory nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition, or
constitutional override. Parent and child definitions remain independent until
`composition` explicitly relates them.

value.label: Recursive discovery and explicit composition

value.definition: Conformance under an exact selected basis covering uniquely resolved uses and material collisions, including distinct Frame, Owner, Product and Tenant contexts and unresolved User meanings absent downstream definition or explicit relation.

grounding.quote:
Conformance covers both uniquely resolved use and material collision. At
minimum, it establishes these cases under an exact selected basis:

value.label: Semantic-resolution conformance

value.definition: STDO-SURFACE-001 chooses one complete released method cut admitted by release authority and one owning standard per law. Authorship is modular; operative authority is singular. A released cut identifies exact members, digests, review basis, human acceptance and immutable identity.

grounding.quote:
The shared methodology is modular in authorship and singular in authority.
Each law has one owning standard; other standards consume it by reference. The
standards become operative only as one complete released STDO version.

value.label: One constitutional surface and version boundary

value.definition: The homeostatic chain runs Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Realisation → Observations → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap Analysis → intake-selected re-entry or observation. Goals select current concerns; Intent gives purpose; mutable Product Definition gives terms and decomposable end-state shape; Requirements state invariant obligations; Design selects structures and delivery; ADRs are design records; Realisation includes software and human procedures; Observations record bounded facts; Projection presents relevant observations; Delta exposes drift; Scenarios test operational meaning; Gap Analysis locates insufficiency.

grounding.quote:
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Realisation → Observations → Projection → Delta
                                                                                       ↓
                                                                                  Scenarios
                                                                                       ↓
                                                                                Gap Analysis
                                                                                       ↓
                                                                  Intake-selected re-entry or observation

value.label: Constitutional chain

value.definition: A bounded execution-control surface under existing constitutional authority, capable of batching work and local compliance escrow; neither a new constitutional layer nor automatic acceptance.

grounding.quote:
A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface.

It is not a new layer in the constitutional chain.

value.label: Sprint execution boundary

value.definition: SPEC_METHOD owns the substrate-neutral ambiguity-governance context. Major ambiguity materially changes architecture, stack, Product boundary, execution/deployment admissibility, public contracts or downstream realization law; micro ambiguity stays within governed design. Lawful Probabilistic Processing is policy-permitted bounded non-human handling of declared ambiguity; Human Adjudication is authority-admitted explicit human judgment where policy or risk requires it. Handling labels and resolution, lawful-decision, admissibility and fulfillment predicates remain distinct.

grounding.quote:
**Lawful Probabilistic Processing**
(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing`) is
bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or resolve
declared ambiguity. **Human Adjudication**
(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication`) is explicit human
judgment admitted by authority to resolve declared ambiguity where policy or
risk appetite requires it.

value.label: Ambiguity governance

value.definition: Every material Product, application, module, graph function, runtime/plugin/public/data surface or capability has an operational lifecycle: intent → requirement → build → assurance → release → deployment → live usage → observed telemetry → retirement.

grounding.quote:
Any material product, application, module, graph function, runtime surface,
plugin surface, public interface, data surface, or capability has an operational
lifecycle.

value.label: Operational lifecycle

value.definition: Substantive change has an explicit declared intent, intake classification and lawful entry into the constitutional chain.

grounding.quote:
Every substantive change begins with intake triage, an explicit declared change
intent, and a lawful re-entry point into the constitutional chain.

value.label: Substantive change

value.definition: The common intake route for bugs, feature requests, issues, regressions, operator findings, release blockers and scenario failures. It diagnoses current failing or changing relations and selects lawful classes: goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice, design_reframe and realization_refactor.

grounding.quote:
There is one front door for substantive change.

The intake label does not determine the process class.

value.label: Universal intake triage

conditions: Assurance or intake requires causal diagnosis of a counterexample on a declared path.
value.definition: Localization finds the earliest evidence-supported causal frontier: one violated locus, a jointly necessary set of incomparable minimal violated loci, unresolved alternative frontiers, or indeterminate when no bounded frontier is supported. Earliest is causal minimality, not log or clock order.
exceptions: It does not add a separate pass to every change.

grounding.quote:
A testing counterexample is returned to its earliest supported causal frontier
on the declared path. The frontier contains the causally minimal violated owner
relations or seam coordinates established by the evidence; earliest means
minimal under the declared causal relation, not first in log or clock order.

value.label: Counterexample localization

value.definition: Reusable intake classification distinguishes C, reproducible facts and declared rule application; J, residual semantic or materiality judgment; and O, rulings reserved to actual owners. These are annotations, not new calculus kinds, runtime interfaces, mandatory documents or authority grants. Computation exposes authority traversal, public delta, accepted-design coverage and rule-determined treatment.

grounding.quote:
`C` denotes reproducible facts and declared
rule application; `J` denotes residual semantic or materiality judgment; `O`
denotes a ruling reserved to its actual owner. These annotations grant no
authority and introduce no calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface, or
mandatory document.

value.label: Computed classification and treatment

value.definition: Closure of a declared change span evaluates all applicable obligations and required judgments or rulings together, with no active non-closure condition. This conjunction differs from local artifact fitness.

grounding.quote:
Closure of a declared change span applies
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) to reliance
on its closure evidence, then evaluates the conjunction of all applicable
obligations and required judgments or rulings, with no active non-closure
condition.

value.label: Consistency gate

value.definition: A Product-outcome-bearing work wave selects one unresolved, directly verifiable Product-defined outcome instance and acceptance interval. Material advance, prerequisite readiness, preservation and regression are progress annotations on distinct predicates. Named bounded prerequisites and decision-discriminating experiments are provisional bases, distinct from Product progress or closure.

grounding.quote:
Every Product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected,
unresolved, directly verifiable Product-defined outcome and declares the
acceptance interval for that instance. Product-progress claims and promotion
onto the supported Product path are judged against that same outcome.

value.label: Product outcome and bounded work basis

value.definition: Proportionality compares material semantic ambiguity removed with effective reasoning complexity introduced. Complexity includes concepts, authority surfaces, document joins, exceptions, branches, states, transitions, duplicated representations and decision detail, rather than raw size. Delivery priority applies this relation to the current outcome, likelihood, impact, reversibility, dependency and feedback delay.

grounding.quote:
Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and
effective reasoning complexity introduced. A method obligation is proportional
when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space justifies the
additional concepts, relations, projections, and evidence that an agent must
hold together to reach a correct decision.

value.label: Proportional method and delivery

conditions: A selected outcome, delegated affected cone, concrete execution binding and separately bound assessment and decision authority exist.
value.definition: UP-020 describes outcome-driven construction through accepted basis, bounded affected relations, selected computational relations, delegated authority, construction/self-review, required independent live assessment, accept/local repair/re-enter/reject, exact accepted checkpoint and next already-authorized action.

grounding.quote:
This family assumes a selected outcome, a delegated affected cone, a concrete
execution binding and separately bound assessment and decision authority.

value.label: Agentic construction execution

value.definition: The sufficient intake binding for a proposed bounded action identifies the outcome/prerequisite/experiment, affected relations and invariants, admitted transformations, computational or common-library dispositions, construction and assessment authority, and upstream re-entry conditions.
value.label: Sufficient execution intake

value.definition: The execution unit is the smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable of delivering selected behavior while preserving every affected governing relation.

grounding.quote:
the
smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable of delivering the selected
behavior while preserving every affected governing relation. Its material seams
follow that condition, not function, file, module, ticket or document boundaries.

value.label: Bounded causal construction

value.definition: Construction, independent assessment and bounded proxy decision are distinct roles. The constructor owns implementation and self-review; the assessor examines exact live realization and evidence; an authorized proxy has only its declared decision envelope.

grounding.quote:
The constructor owns bounded implementation and self-review. Apply
[Independent assessment](FOUNDATIONS.md#independent-assessment) wherever
independent assessment supports promotion. The assessor evaluates the exact
live realisation
under the selected computational binding, its authority paths, proof, and
installed subject rather than treating the constructor's summary as sufficient
evidence. The selected configuration binds actors to that claim under the shared
independence conditions; this construction binding prescribes no actor count.

value.label: Construction, assessment and delegation

value.definition: Assessment of whether an exact candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation returns evidence and a proposed semantic disposition. Applied disposition is a separate decision under bound authority; candidate availability is another construction predicate.

grounding.quote:
Assessment evaluates the exact predicate `the candidate closes its declared
cone and preserves every affected governing relation` through the shared
[result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra). It returns evidence and a
proposed semantic disposition. Apply [Dispose](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#dispose)
to the separate decision on that proposal, using this section's construction
conditions and the existing authority's bound mandate.

value.label: Proportional disposition

value.definition: A consumer-represented read model identifying exact candidate, affected relations, changed realization and authority paths, retained/open seams, focused and required integration proof, explicit non-changes, proposed disposition and separately applied decision.

grounding.quote:
Transition
evidence is a read model and does not become specification, design, or
admission authority.

value.label: Transition evidence and proof cadence

value.definition: Acceptance binds an exact checkpoint. A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted work under an exact existing operation grant without acceptance, promotion or publication. Progress and churn are semantic categories: accepted material outcome movement versus rejected or superseded construction history/cost.

grounding.quote:
A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted work under an
existing exact operation grant. Identify its parent or predecessor, included
territory, concurrent-writer disposition and durable evidence location. It is
neither acceptance, promotion nor publication.

value.label: Checkpoint, continuation, progress and churn

conditions: A consequential transition has actual admission owners.
value.definition: UP-021 admission assesses the exact complete material transition at one current authoritative basis, covering every participant and equality join capable of affecting or being affected by identity, validity, authority, currentness or transition. Assessed admission, authorized decision, actual semantic commit and atomicity are separate claims.

grounding.quote:
Its support universe is
every participant and equality join whose identity, validity, authority,
currentness or transition can affect or be affected by admission. The owner
independently derives and validates that relation from authoritative inputs;
the shared Support condition governs crossing seams and independence claims.

value.label: Complete enclosing-relation admission

value.definition: Standing qualification is instantiated for every admission owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design, with cases applicable to its supported input, state and operating/threat model.

grounding.quote:
Qualification is instantiated for every admission owner and supported boundary
declared by accepted design. Case applicability follows the supported input,
state and operating/threat model. An excluded threat alone cannot create an
acceptance predicate or require defensive work; any proposed scope expansion
returns to its owning authority. Supported malformed inputs, stale state and
effect boundaries retain their required checks:

value.label: Standing structural qualification

value.definition: A core interface is any shared contract or carrier materially governing runtime closure, reporting/status truth, topology/frame progression, proof/qualification outcomes, event/projection semantics, identity/binding resolution or provider/resolver behavior. A change capable of altering how multiple surfaces decide current truth is a core-interface change.

grounding.quote:
If changing the interface can alter how multiple surfaces decide "what is true
now," it is a core interface change.

value.label: Core interface

conditions: A change alters a load-bearing shared interface on which multiple surfaces depend.
value.definition: Constitutional migration replaces shared contract authority across producers, consumers and views, with hard-break sequencing, re-adoption, path-relative promotion and final retirement; it is not an ordinary local patch or automatic deletion rule.

grounding.quote:
Where a change alters a load-bearing contract, carrier, resolver, provider,
projection law, closure law, or other shared interface that multiple surfaces
depend on, the work must be handled as a constitutional migration rather than
as incremental patching.

value.label: Core interface migration

value.definition: Two lawful strategies: Inside-Out Hard-Break replaces authoritative source truth in place on the same implementation line, breaking and repairing outward; Fundamental Re-Adoption intentionally re-derives a major rewrite on a materially different runtime/carrier/type/execution/realization basis and moves the predecessor sideways as reference, not live authority. Bounded evolution is a strategy-selection presumption, not a third strategy.

grounding.quote:
- **Inside-Out Hard-Break Migration**: use this when the project remains on the
  same implementation line and the authoritative source truth is being replaced
  in place. The work proceeds from source carrier outward through a sequence of
  deliberate breaks and repairs.
- **Fundamental Re-Adoption Migration**: use this when the rewrite is major and
  the project is intentionally re-deriving itself on a materially different
  implementation basis, such as a new runtime model, carrier model, type
  system, execution substrate, or realization tree. The prior implementation is
  moved sideways and treated as reference material, not live authority.

value.label: Constitutional migration strategies

value.definition: An immutable operative release cut bounds the feature set accepted at that point and belongs to release metadata and evaluation, distinct from discovery and current constitutional or shared-realization surfaces.

grounding.quote:
The immutable
cut bounds the feature set accepted at that point and belongs to release
metadata and evaluation. Active constitutional and shared realization surfaces
describe current truth by role, boundary and status rather than release-line
branding. Release criteria, publication and advancement remain Release Method's
decisions.

value.label: Release version boundary

value.definition: Evidence establishes only its bound property. Claim owners supply property and scope; authorized evaluators provide evidence rather than replacement targets. The evidence family distinguishes proof-target adequacy, semantic/evidence/projection separation and composite assurance qualification.

grounding.quote:
The claim owner supplies the property and required scope; the
authorized evaluator supplies evidence, not a substitute target.

value.label: Evidence rules

conditions: The proof is load-bearing.
value.definition: An exact proof target binds subject, intended property, governing basis, witness-to-claim relation, nearest weaker excluded property and falsification condition; evidence discovery lacking these is not closure-grade proof.

grounding.quote:
Before selecting that witness, bind its relation to the claim, the nearest
weaker excluded property and the falsification condition. Missing these
relations leaves evidence discovery, not closure-grade proof.

value.label: Proof target identity and adequacy

value.definition: Semantic basis consists of constitutional and accepted-design relations defining meaning; evidence basis comprises exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations evaluating it; state projection is a current view derived from admitted semantic and evidence bases.

grounding.quote:
- **semantic basis**: constitutional and accepted-design relations defining
  what a claim means;
- **evidence basis**: exact artifacts, events, logs, tests, and observations
  used to evaluate it; and
- **state projection**: a current view derived from admitted semantic and
  evidence bases.

value.label: Semantic, evidence and projection bases

value.definition: Assurance evaluates the authoritative composite subject for a claimed promotion or closure predicate. Generic method qualification uses a fresh competent constructor within a declared capability/context/configuration envelope, ordinary declared method and authority surfaces, and an independently authorized evaluator with a declared basis and comparison predicate.

grounding.quote:
Its support boundary is the authoritative composite subject;
single-carrier evidence leaves unexamined cross-carrier obligations open.

value.label: Assurance-boundary congruence and method qualification

value.definition: Requirements preserve invariant truth; Design preserves structural choice; Scenarios preserve operational meaning. Scenarios are concrete end-to-end Product-owner use cases testing the chain from intent to realized behavior.

grounding.quote:
| **Requirements** | Invariant truth | "What must be true?" |
| **Design** | Structural choice | "How is that truth realized?" |
| **Scenarios** | Operational meaning | "Can the realized system actually do the claimed thing?" |

value.label: Verification layers

value.definition: SPEC_METHOD owns Product-level product-assurance taxonomy while DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD retains module-derived unit-proof authority. Two primary authority classes are design/module conformance, derived from realization law, and UAT/acceptance, derived from constitutional Product authority. Execution breadth is separate. Sandbox UAT is composed-product acceptance; harnessed/fake/recorded/deterministic execution is non-live, while live requires real external worker or transport execution.

grounding.quote:
Authority source is not the same thing as execution breadth. A test may be
small or broad, fast or slow, deterministic or live, but it still derives from
one of two primary authorities:

1. **Design/module conformance tests**
2. **UAT / acceptance tests**

value.label: Testing strategy taxonomy

value.definition: Proof-fixture portability makes required closure lanes reproducible from their declared source boundary while distinguishing fixture availability from the Product property under evaluation.

grounding.quote: Required closure lanes must be reproducible from the declared source boundary.

value.label: Fixture and proof portability

value.definition: Written traceable testcase authority for live requirements may take the form of scenario bundles, ordered sequences, negative/control cases or other explicit evidence cases appropriate to the truth being proved.

grounding.quote:
That authority may include scenario bundles, ordered testcase sequences, negative
or control cases, and other explicit evidence cases as appropriate to the kind of
truth being proved, but it must exist in written form and be traceable.

value.label: Test authority

value.definition: A scenario bundle or equivalent ordered testcase set makes operational meaning inspectable through a coherent feature/use-case boundary, proving sequence and expected significant-step outcomes. Declared scenarios identify operational boundaries, actors, controls and significant paths and pressure feature intent and design.

grounding.quote:
Where a requirement claims meaningful system behavior, the proving surface should
be a scenario bundle or equivalent ordered set of testcases that exercises that
behavior through a coherent sequence rather than as disconnected fragments.

value.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The system has an installable or runnable development form.
value.definition: The decisive proof lane exercises an installed development version as an independent project or externalized target, beyond in-place source-tree checks.

grounding.quote:
Where a system has an installable or runnable development form, the decisive
proving lane runs against an installed development version as if it were an
independent project or externalized target, not only against the source tree in
place.

value.label: Installed development proof

value.definition: Significant paths are the meaningful paths of claimed behavior, usually including applicable success, rejection/fail-closed, boundary/control, integration/dispatch/transport and recovery/retry/replay paths. Exhaustive proof here means intentional proof of declared meaningful paths, not every branch in every file.

grounding.quote:
Exhaustive proof does not mean every possible branch in every file. It means the
project names the meaningful paths and proves them intentionally.

value.label: Significant path coverage

value.definition: Four constitutional requirement categories classify asserted truth: Capability supplies behavior/function/surface; Constraint or Guarantee bounds behavior through invariants/laws/safety/portability/semantics; Governance controls lifecycle/authority/visibility/release/operator action; Verification requires tests/evidence/traceability/qualification/forensics. Category is neither priority nor user-facing status.

grounding.quote:
| **Capability** | A behavior, function, or surface the system must provide | "What can the system do?" |
| **Constraint / Guarantee** | An invariant, law, safety property, portability rule, or semantic guarantee that bounds how the system may behave | "What must always remain true?" |
| **Governance** | A policy or control rule over lifecycle, authority, visibility, release, or operator action | "What governs use and change?" |
| **Verification** | A requirement on tests, evidence, traceability, qualification, or forensic surfaces | "How do we know the claim is true?" |

value.label: Requirement categories

value.definition: Specification-driven reconstruction is sufficient ordered derivability by a competent team: Goals to conformant Intent, Intent to Product, Product to Requirements, Requirements to Design, and Requirements plus Design to Realization in its selected environment. Sufficiency does not require unique, deterministic or identical realizations.

grounding.quote:
This does not mean the derivation is unique. Different designs may satisfy the
same requirements, and different software, human or mixed realizations may
satisfy the same design. The test is sufficiency, not determinism.

value.label: Reconstruction litmus

value.definition: Requirements state which control or delivery surfaces must exist; Design chooses their concrete mechanisms, including unconstrained stack, carrier, runtime, entry documents, embedded blocks, compiled artifacts or other lawful topology.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state what control or delivery surfaces must exist.

Design decides the concrete mechanism that realizes them.

If a technology stack, carrier, or runtime is not already constrained by an
upstream constitutional surface, choosing it is part of design rather than a
separate upstream authority.

value.label: Design realization choice

value.definition: Cumulative renewal from current specification through real use, gap analysis and intake-selected re-entry or observation. Requirements and design are refined, realization is repeatedly re-derived, and implementation, testing, replay and scenario gaps feed repricing while constitutional authority retains its direction.

grounding.quote: Current spec → real-world use case → gap analysis → intake-selected re-entry or observation

value.label: Renewal Path

value.definition: Constitutional trace closure connects live obligations with owning realization or explicit unresolved/deferred relations and closes constitutional authority over realized behavior; it exceeds documentation completeness.

grounding.quote:
a live
obligation needs an owning realization or an explicit unresolved/deferred
relation, and historical evidence cannot change current authority.

value.label: Constitutional trace closure

conditions: The domain artifact has been published as a live constitutional surface.
value.definition: Versioned constitutional history, immutable in place. Multiple live domain surfaces may accumulate. Mutable implementation surfaces have a different status.

grounding.quote: - Live domain artifacts, once published as live constitutional surfaces, are immutable in place.

value.label: Live constitutional surface

conditions: A project intentionally abandons its prior constitutional shape and re-derives itself on a new branch, version line or methodology basis.
value.definition: A constitutional reset through controlled adoption. Inherited documents become source material; absence from the new surface means not yet adopted. Implementation classifications are carry_across: materially unchanged and intentionally re-adopted; redundant: no longer needed; rewrite: needed but rebuilt under new requirements and design.

grounding.quote:
A fundamental migration is a constitutional reset, not an in-place refactor.

This rule applies when a project intentionally abandons a prior constitutional shape and re-derives itself on a new branch, version line, or methodology basis.

value.label: Fundamental migration

value.definition: The recommended understanding of refactor and migration as a wave over mutable implementation surfaces, with an in-flight state, declared affected scope and landing boundary.

grounding.quote:
Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over
mutable implementation surfaces.

value.label: Transformation wave

value.definition: Lifecycle classification domain: Deferred retains an explicitly not-yet-operative or not-yet-realized live obligation; Superseded means ownership moved to a newer constitutional surface or design decision; Active remains current live constitutional law; Orphaned is no longer part of the intended system.

grounding.quote:
| **Deferred** | Retained in the live surface as an explicit not-yet-operative or not-yet-realized obligation | Keep with an honest deferment surface and do not present as current closure |
| **Superseded** | Ownership has moved to a newer constitutional surface or design decision | Add Implements/Supersedes to the governing design record |
| **Active** | Remains live constitutional law in the current surface | Must have an owning design decision — write or update one |
| **Orphaned** | No longer part of the intended system | Remove or explicitly supersede |

value.label: Requirement lifecycle status

value.definition: Independent requirement-kind axis with values Capability, Constraint / Guarantee, Governance and Verification; it identifies the kind of project truth asserted, rather than lifecycle membership or operativity.

grounding.quote:
2. **Requirement category**
   - Capability
   - Constraint / Guarantee
   - Governance
   - Verification

value.label: Requirement category

value.definition: Constitutional layer orienting the current bounded work wave.

grounding.quote: **Goals** orient the current bounded work wave.

value.label: Goals

value.definition: Constitutional layer stating why the system exists and which directional changes are inside or outside scope.

grounding.quote: **Intent** states why the system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope.

value.label: Intent

value.definition: Current concrete Product-definition layer bridging Intent to Requirements.

grounding.quote: **Product** states the current concrete product definition and bridges intent to requirements.

value.label: Product specification

value.definition: Stable obligations that must be true, with acceptance criteria and sufficient meaning for downstream design derivation.

grounding.quote: **Requirements** state stable obligations that must be true.

value.label: Requirements

value.definition: Downstream structural HOW realizing requirement truth, including choices of structure, interfaces, carriers, packaging and tenant boundaries.

grounding.quote: **Design** states how requirement truth is realized. It is downstream of requirements and may choose structure, interfaces, carriers, packaging, and tenant boundaries.

value.label: Design

value.definition: Realized behavior repeatedly derived against the current constitutional surface; its governing basis comprises Requirements together with Design.

grounding.quote: requirements plus design govern realisation

value.label: Realisation

value.definition: ADR: durable design memory organized by the decision making acceptance criteria true, rather than by requirement-file boundaries; not a second requirement surface.

grounding.quote: **ADRs** are durable design memory. They are not a second requirement surface.

value.label: Architecture decision record

value.definition: Product Definition copied from the selected cut's PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json, named stdo_default.json for a singleton default or stdo_<label>.json for a named definition. URI bindings choose actual carriers. Defaults bind the shared exact STDO basis; specification/GOALS.md, INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md and requirements/; build_tenants/common and default; and .ai-workspace/sprints, tickets/{backlog,active,completed}, and comments.

grounding.quote:
Every STDO-defined product begins from
`templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json`. Copy it to the product's
definition root as `stdo_default.json` for a singleton default project or as
`stdo_<label>.json` for a named product definition. An existing project fills
the URI bindings over its current layout; adoption does not require moving,
renaming, or duplicating existing authority or realization surfaces.

value.label: Product Definition bootstrap

value.definition: Source-described intake, feature-change, bootstrap/repricing and use-case-gap procedures that select lawful constitutional re-entry before dependent realization.

grounding.quote:
1. Triage the intake and classify the change.
2. Determine the lawful re-entry point into the constitutional chain.
3. Identify the affected downstream span that must remain consistent.
4. Only then treat the work as implementation, repricing, or release-bound change.

value.label: Method procedure

value.definition: The document titled STDO Reference Frame Baseline; an optional specialized role and evaluation profile. Its profile mappings are distinct from pure frame law and Product-owned adoption.

grounding.quote: # STDO Reference Frame Baseline

This document is an optional specialized role and evaluation profile. “Derived”
in its frame headings means an application of shared law with the additional
profile choices identified below, not a uniquely forced role inventory. It has no
independent ownership of STDO's execution protocol or of any Product binding.

value.label: STDO Reference Frame Baseline

value.definition: Heading organizing the profile's terminology; it contributes no independent operational rule.

grounding.quote: ## Profile Terms

value.label: Profile Terms

value.definition: A REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD frame evaluating selection, construction, assessment or disposition of governed work. This profile's engagement frames are Executive, Worker and Reviewer.

grounding.quote:
An **engagement frame** is a `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` frame whose evaluation
family concerns selection, construction, assessment, or disposition of governed
work. Executive, Worker, and Reviewer are this profile's engagement frames.

value.label: Engagement frame

conditions: Needed by one engagement evaluation and activated with declared evaluation, basis, material manifold, authority, evidence, result algebra and capability envelope.
value.definition: A Product, requirement, design, identity, release, domain, implementation, test, operational, historical or capability frame. A method member, file, component or lens becomes a frame only through the stated declaration.

grounding.quote:
A **specialist frame** is an activated Product, requirement, design, identity,
release, domain, implementation, test, operational, historical, or capability
frame needed by one engagement evaluation. A method member, file, component, or
lens becomes a frame only when its evaluation, basis, material manifold,
authority, evidence, result algebra, and capability envelope are declared.

value.label: Specialist frame

value.definition: Reusable evaluation archetype whose recurring distinction must be instantiated where material, established non-material by capable authority, or retained as an explicit coverage residual. It selects no concrete carrier, component, actor, architecture, owner or implementation.

grounding.quote:
A **generic specialist-frame family** is a reusable evaluation-family
archetype in this profile. It identifies a recurring distinction that a
project must either instantiate it where material, have capable authority
establish it as non-material for the governed outcome, or retain it as an
explicit coverage residual.

value.label: Generic specialist-frame family

conditions: Evaluation executes or observes a declared subject against one exact claim with an explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification condition.
value.definition: A claim-bounded specialist frame for testing. Files, suites, runners, fixtures, scenario labels, coverage percentages and actors are not testing frames merely by existing. Counts, coverage, duration and framework category do not enlarge its authority.

grounding.quote:
Testing-frame authority is bounded by the claim actually exercised. Test count,
assertion count, source coverage, runtime duration, and framework category do
not widen that boundary.

value.label: Testing frame

value.definition: Declared ordinary causal composition from supported user or Public entry through the exact interfaces, owners, state transitions, effects, persistence/recovery boundaries and outcome projection required by the Product claim. Equal output through a bypass, obsolete executor, test-only seam, undeclared fallback or competing authority falsifies path conformance.

grounding.quote:
Producing an expected output
through a bypass, obsolete executor, test-only seam, undeclared fallback, or
competing authority falsifies path conformance even when the output value is
equal.

value.label: Authoritative Product path

value.definition: Claim-relative independent dimensions and interactions whose combinations can change outcomes, violate invariants, select authority paths or expose failure. Unit dimensions are module-owned laws, public contracts, algebraic operators, calculation regimes, states, transitions, boundaries and failures. Cross-participant interface, Product, persistence, configuration and user-role combinations belong to integration, end-to-end or user-acceptance evidence; mocking them does not make them unit evidence.

grounding.quote:
Cross-participant
interface, Product, persistence, configuration, and user-role combinations
belong to integration, end-to-end, or user-acceptance frames rather than being
mocked away and counted as unit evidence.

value.label: Material combinatorial complexity

conditions: The coordinated branch is selected under existing project authority.
value.definition: Frame selecting or confirming bounded activations and consuming closed Worker/Reviewer results. It maintains enough long-term outcome, MVP/release mandate, unresolved obligations, dependencies and exact results to prioritize, dispose and select authorized action. The workspace holds the durable frontier; full Product/history/private worker context need not be loaded. Occupants may be direct human authority or an admitted bounded proxy, not a universal semantic owner, controller, manager service or runtime observer.

grounding.quote:
The underlying workspace carries the durable frontier; the Executive need not
load the whole Product, every historical result or every worker's context.

value.label: Executive

value.definition: Basis for one Product or an explicit directed Product chain, distinguishing every mutable Source Project, current Product Definition, candidate checkpoint, Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product and composition edge. Each Development Product binds one exact underlying Install; each edge records source/target roles, authority, contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and invalidation.

grounding.quote:
Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying Install
identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, governing authority and
contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal, and invalidation.

value.label: Product-chain basis

conditions: Activated as a reference frame through sufficient admitted intake.
value.definition: STDO-UP-020 bounded constructor owning construction and self-review through the governing work relation's inherited operation authority. This role does not acquire admission, publication, acceptance or continuation authority.

grounding.quote:
**Worker** is the profile label for `STDO-UP-020`'s bounded constructor role
when activated as a reference frame. It owns construction and self-review
inside its exact intake through the operation authority inherited from the
governing work relation. It does not acquire admission, publication, acceptance,
or continuation authority.

value.label: Worker / Writer

conditions: Activated as a reference frame for independent live-surface evaluation.
value.definition: Independent evaluation consumed by STDO-UP-020 assessment and governed by STDO-UP-007 and STDO-UP-022. It evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result, with evidence-bound technical triage when findings exist; it does not repair, prioritize, dispose or activate another frame.

grounding.quote:
evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result with evidence-bound
technical triage when a finding exists. It does not implement the repair,
assign priority, apply disposition, or activate the next frame.

value.label: Reviewer

value.definition: Reviewer-owned assessment of a finding against its exact claim and basis: affected claim/failure, Product-scale severity, causal assessment/confidence, blast radius/users/paths/relations, workaround/containment, repair complexity/regression risk/dependencies, and uncertainty/reducing evidence, where evidence and capability support them. Severity grades consequence; Executive priority orders response against complete outcome, likelihood/exposure, MVP/release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, delay cost and capacity. Current-boundary effect is Executive's blocks, narrowing or explicit-residual decision.

grounding.quote:
**Severity** grades consequence if the finding manifests. **Priority** orders
response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and exposure,
current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, cost of delay, and
available capacity. Reviewer grades severity. Executive assigns priority.

value.label: Technical triage and decision projections

conditions: Successful lawful Worker activation has occurred.
value.definition: Closed Worker output to its declared consumer, Executive in the coordinated branch. Its exact predicate is availability of the requested candidate and transition evidence on the activated basis within admitted bounds. Variants candidate_ready, refused, incomplete and re_entry_requested refine domain outcomes, not the shared result algebra or semantic dispositions. Every result retains the shared core record and actual performance/effect state.
exceptions: Activation refusal creates neither a Worker activation nor a Worker result.

grounding.quote:
A **work result** is the closed Worker output to its declared consumer; in the
coordinated branch that consumer is Executive. It exists only after successful
Worker activation. An `activation_refusal` returns to the assigning authority
or declared result carrier and creates neither a Worker activation nor a
Worker result.

value.label: Work result

value.definition: Subject identity for STDO-UP-020 transition evidence and STDO-UP-007 review traceability. Where STDO-UP-022 generic-method qualification applies, construction is frozen before material reference exposure as its owner requires; elsewhere an immutable identity or equivalent exact-subject relation stabilizes the assessment. This introduces no constitutional lifecycle state named frozen.

grounding.quote:
This profile does not create a new constitutional lifecycle state named
`frozen`.

value.label: Exact candidate

value.definition: Faithful projection from the Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis into profile engagement, retaining selected mapping, outcome, actor envelopes, evidence coordinates and revision conditions. Adoption remains the source owner's decision.

grounding.quote:
Its material distinctions are the selected mapping,
outcome, actor envelopes, evidence coordinates and revision conditions in
[Adopt This Baseline](#adopt-this-baseline). Adoption remains that source
owner's decision.

value.label: Baseline-adoption projection

value.definition: Three distinct structures: authority precedence for work/configuration/disposition/re-entry; temporal and evidence flow for activation packets and closed results; and frame topology for disjointness, overlap, conjunction, translation or composition. Evaluation independence and Reviewer-assurance independence remain separate activation relations. Alignment or shared basis, outcome, checkpoint, candidate, relations, evidence and residuals does not merge these structures or authorities. An engagement frame plus material specialist set, exact subject/basis and capable actor represents one evaluation without requiring a Cartesian-product schema or universal runtime.

grounding.quote: These structures may align in one case. They are not one hierarchy.

value.label: Non-hierarchical frame configuration

value.definition: Smallest real runnable path from supported Product entry to a material outcome through selected composition, used to sequence early delivery and bounded expansion.

grounding.quote:
Executive sequences delivery around a steel thread: the smallest real,
runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through
the selected composition. Establish that path early and expand it in bounded
increments. Where it already exists, extend or revalidate the affected
thread. Select increments by consequential uncertainty, dependency and
interface reach, and failure impact.

value.label: Steel-thread delivery

value.definition: Evaluation of whether a declared user with admitted capability and information obtains the exact Product outcome through the supported ordinary surface. Basis: exact deployed/installed/runnable Product; current Product, requirements, UX, identity, policy and acceptance authority; user, environment and harnessed/live mode. Coordinates retain Product/artifact/install, user capability, configuration/dependency realization, mode, data/workspace/invocation/time/outcome/scenario. Evidence is supported requests/responses, projections, claimed durable effects, refusals/recovery, scenario and exact dependency identities. Result is one claim-bound frame result with witnessed paths, counterexamples, residual users and invalidators.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Can a declared user, with the user's admitted capability and information, obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the supported ordinary Product surface? |

value.label: User-acceptance frame

value.definition: Evaluation of exact runnable Product outcome through the complete authoritative path, covering every material interface, owner, state/effect/persistence/continuation/recovery/projection boundary and causal producer/consumer. Basis includes composition design, supported entry, selected owners/dependencies and ordinary runtime configuration. Coordinates preserve artifact/installed tree, entry/operation/definition/owner, path/edges/process/event prefix/state/configuration/dependency/result/replay/scenario. Evidence includes entry invocation, semantic path/authority edges, owner receipts, durable events, transitions, outputs, claimed replay/reconstruction, installed identity and negative paths. Result retains exercised edges, unexercised paths, counterexamples and residual combinations.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Does the exact Product subject realize the claimed outcome through the complete authoritative Product path, including every material interface, owner, state transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery, and projection boundary? |

value.label: End-to-end frame

value.definition: Evaluation of actual participants at one material composition boundary against their joint contract over consequential state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery combinations. Basis includes exact interface/composition, actual implementations or claim-admitted exact substitutes, governing Product/requirement/design law and interaction population. Both sides, shared carriers, pre/postconditions, ownership/order/state/configuration/failure/retry/recovery/translation and competitors are material. Coordinates retain participant/version/interface/carrier/state/configuration/dependency/case/input/output/failure/evidence identity. Evidence comprises actual exchanges, admitted carriers, transitions, contract verdicts and interaction/failure/recovery observations; result retains covered and omitted interactions, counterexamples and invalidators.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Do the actual participants at one declared material composition boundary satisfy their joint contract across the combinations of state, authority, configuration, timing, failure, and recovery that can change the boundary result? |

value.label: Integration frame

value.definition: Evaluation of one exact module-owned law across material algebraic operators, calculation regimes, states/transitions, public/private boundary classes and failures. Basis includes accepted Ontology/design, active IACS or equivalent inventory, module requirements/public contracts, implementation and a module-bounded decidable oracle. Manifold includes contracts, algebras/calculations/parsers/reducers/state machines/transition functions/combinators/admission predicates/conservation/invariants/numerical boundaries/failures. Coordinates preserve module/implementation revision, law/operator/function family/state/input/boundary/expected relation/generated case/mutation/result. Evidence includes law-derived examples/classes, available finite exhaustive cases, generative/property/metamorphic cases, independent oracles, boundaries and killed internal mutations; result remains limited to that law/population with counterexamples, residual combinations and invalidators.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Does one module-owned law hold across its material combinations of algebraic operator, calculation regime, state, transition, public or private boundary class, and failure case? |

value.label: Unit-test frame

value.definition: Claim-relative testing value indexed first by discriminated material combinations. At least eight dimensions: subject congruence, number/materiality of independent dimensions, covered interaction strength, authoritative-path exactness, oracle independence/precision, realistic-fault/rival-path/historical-failure sensitivity, observability/reconstruction/reproducibility, and explicit residual combinations/invalidators. Local value normally rises with module combinatorial complexity; broader value can be multiplicative through interactions, without asserting probability or statistical independence.
value.label: Testing-value index

value.definition: A Product path claim concerns both exact reachability of each required authoritative composition through the ordinary supported runnable Product path and exclusion of each material forbidden production path.

grounding.quote: Every Product path claim requires two-sided evidence:

value.label: Product path claim

value.definition: Testing evidence comprises distinct user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration and unit claims. Their default responsibilities are respectively the supported user's outcome, the complete authoritative runnable Product path, material participant composition and module-owned laws.
value.label: Testing evidence

value.definition: Assurance acquisition and evaluation distinguish the actual owner-issued subject from an independently derived oracle grounded in Product, requirements and accepted design. Assertion provenance and execution provenance are separate.

grounding.quote:
actual owner-issued subject and an independently derived oracle from Product,
requirements and accepted design.

value.label: Assurance subject and independent oracle

value.definition: Counterexample localization is a bounded application of Spec's causal-frontier evaluation to an exact testing subject, declared causal path, owner relations and seams; its result remains separate from the original testing result.

grounding.quote:
Preserve the original testing result alongside the
localization result

value.label: Counterexample localization

value.definition: urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1 is a composite refinement in urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation, acquired from the named heading under the exact selected baseline. It relates Public Boundary, Design, Operator, Owner and Proof to Integration, End To End and User Acceptance. It asks whether one outcome remains constructable, understandable and correctly realized across its material interface chain with sufficient context and conserved meaning, authority and cause. It adds no generic family, testing type, role or universal activation gate.

grounding.quote:
`urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1` is a composite
refinement in `urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation`.

value.label: End-to-end interface integration frame

value.definition: Four distinct interface claims are contract sufficiency (each participant can determine and perform its responsibility from declared interface and context), boundary congruence (selected participants preserve domains, meaning, lifecycle and authority), path realization (the exact runnable subject follows the authoritative entry-to-outcome path), and user usability (the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtains the outcome through declared context, access and supported surface).

grounding.quote: | User usability | Can the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtain the selected outcome using only its declared context, access and supported surface? Internal success or validator-aware fixtures cannot establish this claim. |

value.label: Four interface claim boundaries

value.definition: The selected engagement configuration distinguishes a coordinated branch from direct Worker engagement. Direct engagement retains sufficient intake, work-result refinement, closure conditions and owner boundaries without inserting an Executive appointment or an inapplicable review.

grounding.quote:
Direct Worker engagement preserves the same sufficient intake,
work-result refinement, closure conditions and owner boundaries without inserting
Executive appointment or a review that no applicable condition requires.

value.label: Engagement configuration

value.definition: Executive is the coordinated-branch consumer and activator described here: it binds Worker intake, evaluates returned work and required assessment, and disposes only within existing authority. This local identity does not reconstruct the omitted full Executive frame declaration.

grounding.quote:
Executive binds the [Derived Worker Frame](#derived-worker-frame) and
[Baseline-Specific Activation Additions](#baseline-specific-activation-additions)
to the `STDO-UP-020` sufficient execution intake

value.label: Executive

value.definition: Worker is the bounded activated work producer whose completed coordinated activation returns Work result refinement and STDO-UP-020 transition evidence to Executive; direct work uses its declared consumer.

grounding.quote:
Every completed coordinated Worker activation returns the
[Work result](#work-result) refinement and `STDO-UP-020` transition evidence
to Executive through [Handoff Projection](#handoff-projection). Direct work
uses its declared consumer.

value.label: Worker

value.definition: Reviewer returns an RF-012 closed result with exact subject, population, independence, assurance-path and invalidation coordinates; findings, counterexamples, adjacent observations and re-entry ownership pass through triage and handoff to Executive.

grounding.quote:
Reviewer returns [RF-012's closed result](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results)
with the Derived Reviewer Frame's exact subject, population, independence,
assurance-path and invalidation coordinates.

value.label: Reviewer

value.definition: Finding-level triage has complete, indeterminate and not_applicable payload classifications, distinct from core verdicts, dispositions, priorities and lifecycle states. Core review verdicts are satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis.

grounding.quote:
`complete`, `indeterminate`, and `not_applicable` below classify
the finding-level triage payload; they are not new evaluation results,
dispositions, priorities, or lifecycle states.

value.label: Review verdict and triage domains

value.definition: Handoff Projection transports source-contract bindings to named consumers while preserving materially distinct candidate, process, episode, configuration, evidence-population and basis identities. Existing admitted work carriers can hold those bindings.

grounding.quote:
The exact candidate,
process, episode, configuration, evidence population and basis remain distinct
where material; required equality or translation uses the Frame Method.

value.label: Handoff Projection

value.definition: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis projects existing authority's outcome, work and configuration decisions and cites their material sources; it is not an independent local-axiom authority.

grounding.quote: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis projects that decision.

value.label: Project Reference-Frame Basis

value.definition: Product-owned adoption or project-defined configuration names the document's choice between adopting the optional baseline and defining a project configuration under existing authorities.

grounding.quote: ## Product-Owned Adoption Or Project-Defined Configuration

value.label: Baseline adoption or project-defined configuration

value.definition: Profile qualification evaluates the derived profile and its declared composition with the exact Reference Frame Method basis under Frame Qualification and STDO-UP-022. Mechanical document checks and capable source-linked semantic review are different evidence kinds.

grounding.quote:
Mechanical document checks may protect exact table shape, result cardinality,
source-digest congruence, and named refusal boundaries. They do not establish
semantic truth or replace a capable source-linked Reviewer evaluation.

value.label: Profile qualification

value.definition: Ticket Method is a work-carrier member binding shared transformations to durable work identity, admission, recording and closure. Recoverability beyond private actor memory motivates surviving carriers; tickets, sprints and default layout are additional member policy rather than universal consequences of finite capacity.

grounding.quote:
Tickets, sprints and the default file layout are this member's
additional policy, not universal consequences of finite capacity.

value.label: Ticket Method

value.definition: Goals are the current epic layer located by Product Definition Overlay ticketing.goals, defaulting to GOALS.md. They are broader than a ticket, narrower and more current than INTENT.md, and state the active work wave and current priorities; they are not the durable execution-tracking unit.

grounding.quote: Goals are not the durable unit of execution tracking.

value.label: Goals carrier

conditions: Work needs independent durable identity.
value.definition: A ticket is one enduring, authoritative, typed work record surviving sessions, with one Markdown file as its default carrier. Feature work, bugs, spikes and chores share this system.

grounding.quote: Tickets are used when work needs independent durable identity for:

value.label: Ticket

value.definition: A sprint is a bounded execution batch with one manifest under optional ticketing.sprints.root, default .ai-workspace/sprints/. It batches authority references, closure law, evidence expectations and permitted deferred local compliance debt and closes through explicit sprint-close review. It may contain durable tickets, manifest-local iteration entries or both.

grounding.quote:
A sprint may contain durable tickets, manifest-local iteration entries, or both.
Use tickets for work items that need durable identity across sessions. Use
manifest-local iteration entries for small changes whose only independent value
is traceability inside the sprint.

value.label: Sprint

value.definition: Comments form the discussion/publication message board located by ticketing.comments.root, default .ai-workspace/comments/. They carry ideas, strategy notes, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries, decisions and reasoning. They are not task-status authority; POSTING_GUIDE.md governs publication.

grounding.quote:
Comments are not task status authority. The publication rules for comments are
governed by `POSTING_GUIDE.md`.

value.label: Comments

value.definition: An execution contract is the current run-scoped admitted execution function, derived from a ticket, sprint manifest plus included ticket/iteration, or intake when no durable or sprint-local work identity is needed. It is not a rival backlog or planning surface. Unlike a ticket surviving sessions and waves or a sprint surviving its batch and close review, its scope is one run.

grounding.quote:
Execution contracts are the run-scoped admitted work surface derived from a
ticket, from a sprint manifest plus included ticket or iteration entry, or
drafted during intake when no durable or sprint-local work identity is required.

value.label: Execution contract

value.definition: A closure-bearing milestone has stable identity, a bounded claim, relevant dependencies, current state, required evidence and an explicit relation to ticket closure. Multiple milestones can belong to one ticket without becoming multiple tickets.

grounding.quote:
A ticket may contain several closure-bearing milestones without becoming
several tickets. Each milestone has stable identity, a bounded claim, relevant
dependencies, current state, required evidence, and an explicit relation to
ticket closure.

value.label: Closure-bearing milestone

value.definition: Sprint close review distinguishes item-compliance assessment, authorized treatment decision, actual effects and sprint closure. Treatment values are accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice and remove; they are not core compliance verdicts.

grounding.quote:
These six values classify treatment. The assessment separately evaluates
`this exact item meets the currently applicable compliance obligations under
the sprint and cited domain authority`.

value.label: Sprint close review

value.definition: A Multi-Build-Tenant Work Item is one admitted upstream work item with more than one build-tenant execution line. Its upstream authority and tenant-local tickets have distinct identities and lifecycles. Ticket Method owns this work-item/lifecycle relation within urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy, while Spec owns build-tenant identity and realization meaning.

grounding.quote:
A **Multi-Build-Tenant Work Item** is one admitted upstream work item with more
than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each
tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles.

value.label: Multi-Build-Tenant Work Item

value.definition: Ticket type answers what kind of work record this is. The minimum common set is feature, bug, spike and chore; the source recommends that this default set should suffice for most cases.

grounding.quote: Projects may add more, but this default set should be enough for most cases.

value.label: Ticket type

value.definition: Ticket category identifies execution or migration discipline, independently of ticket type. The minimum common categories are ordinary and implementation_migration. Implementation migration is governed replacement of one implementation truth path across producers, consumers, projections and proof surfaces, including tracker/read-model replacement, public-interface migration and bridge/facade removal.

grounding.quote:
Use `implementation_migration` when the ticket is not just “change code until
tests pass”, but a governed replacement of one implementation truth path with
another across producers, consumers, projections, and proof surfaces.

value.label: Ticket category

value.definition: Change class identifies lawful constitutional re-entry, independently of ticket type and category. Source examples include goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice, design_reframe and realization_refactor; the examples are common pairings rather than exclusive type restrictions.

grounding.quote:
- `change_class` governs lawful constitutional re-entry
- `ticket_category` governs ticket execution and closure discipline

value.label: Change class

value.definition: Recorded residual judgment and owner ruling are distinct reusable evidence/authority records in the existing work carrier. A judgment records a bounded conclusion with evidence and a revising observation; an owner ruling preserves the original mandate and wording separately from agent interpretation. Repricing dispositions retained, superseded, deferred and withdrawn concern authorized treatment of obligations, not delivery fulfillment.

grounding.quote: J is not O; the shared Authority condition governs recording and use.

value.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

value.definition: Condition-based closure evaluates whether every applicable declared obligation of an exact work claim is satisfied and no active non-closure condition remains. Required owner acceptance is its own predicate; evidence about acceptance and the act of accepting remain distinct.

grounding.quote:
`every applicable
declared obligation of this exact work claim is satisfied and no active
non-closure condition remains`

value.label: Condition-based closure

value.definition: Tests are proof projections from admitted work authority. Their expectation authority, interpreted predicate and derivation are distinct from execution provenance identifying the actual subject, checker, environment, observations and result.

grounding.quote: Tests are proof projections from admitted work authority.

value.label: Test case authority

conditions: ticket_category: implementation_migration
value.definition: A ticket category supplying concrete migration declarations, break/closure maps and review evidence to Spec's migration law. It is a ticket-local enforcement surface, not a competing migration policy.

grounding.quote:
This ticket family chooses the concrete
declaration, break/closure map and review checklist; it supplies evidence to
that law, not another migration policy or permission to reinterpret it.

value.label: Implementation migration

value.definition: migration_strategy selects inside_out_hard_break or fundamental_re_adoption. The latter classifies inherited implementation as carry_across, redundant or rewrite.

grounding.quote:
Allowed inherited-implementation classifications are:

- `carry_across`
- `redundant`
- `rewrite`

Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure.

Allowed values are:

- `inside_out_hard_break`
- `fundamental_re_adoption`

value.label: Migration strategy

conditions: Implementation migration ticket
value.definition: library_usage records whether the active boundary rebuilds a pattern locally, consumes a reusable library/commonization surface, or extends that surface before local implementation lands. Its values are none, consume and extend.

grounding.quote:
Implementation migration tickets must declare whether the active boundary is:

- rebuilding a pattern locally
- consuming an existing reusable library/commonization surface
- extending that surface before the local implementation lands

This is what `library_usage` records.

Allowed `library_usage` values are:

- `none`
- `consume`
- `extend`

value.label: Library usage and recurrence

conditions: The same work item is processed across multiple build tenants
Review concerns backlog/active tickets
value.definition: Tenant-local ticket lifecycles, proof surfaces, closure laws and follow-on work remain independently reviewable.

grounding.quote:
1. each tenant has its own suffixed ticket
2. each ticket names its `build_tenant`
3. each tenant ticket has its own proof surface and closure law
4. one tenant's green proof does not stand in for another tenant's closure

value.label: Multi-build-tenant review

value.definition: Ticket-specific functional review distinguishes source-truth migration from renaming, wrapping, adapting or relocating a surviving semantic center.

grounding.quote:
Implementation migration tickets must make the review problem concrete enough
that an implementor cannot land a rename, adapter, wrapper, or happy-path proof
and claim source-truth migration.

value.label: Functional migration review

conditions: Core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration
value.definition: A named walk of every live interface capable of bypassing, reinterpreting, replaying or projecting the migrating truth path, with an interface-specific closure criterion for each item.

grounding.quote:
This checklist is a named walk of every live interface that can still bypass,
reinterpret, replay, or project the migrating truth path.

value.label: Impacted Interface Review Checklist

conditions: Implementation migration touches a core interface
value.definition: Required Break Order is an ordered execution description proceeding outward from authoritative source truth. A Break-To-Closure Map identifies which break closes which closure-law clause when multiple old interfaces exist.

grounding.quote:
The ticket must also include a `Break-To-Closure Map` when the migration has
multiple old interfaces. The map must state which break closes which
closure-law clause. Without that map, partial landing can look like full
landing.

value.label: Required break order and break-to-closure map

conditions: Migration ticket
value.definition: Negative or structural proof addresses whether an old path can still satisfy the closure law; positive behavior proof alone is insufficient.

grounding.quote:
For a migration ticket, positive behavior proof is not enough.

The proof surface should include at least one negative or structural proof that
the old path can no longer satisfy the closure law.

value.label: Mixed-state negative proof

value.definition: The minimum work-carrier states are backlog, active and completed. They are carrier states rather than a second result algebra; claims of valid transitions have their own exact predicates and core results.

grounding.quote:
These values select work-carrier state, not a second result algebra. A claim
that a state transition is valid carries its own core result and exact
predicate.

value.label: Ticket status

value.definition: Product Definition Overlay bindings ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed locate tickets, defaulting respectively to .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/, .ai-workspace/tickets/active/ and .ai-workspace/tickets/completed/. Backlog is accepted durable visible work outside current execution focus; active is the bounded execution set; completed is closed work retained as history. This arrangement keeps active search readable without placing deferred work in comments or goals.

grounding.quote:
- `backlog`: accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part
  of the current execution focus
- `active`: the current bounded execution set
- `completed`: closed work retained as history

Completed tickets move to `ticketing.tickets.lanes.completed`. The default is:

- `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/`

value.label: Ticket lanes

value.definition: UP-009 distinguishes owning work state from its views: Goals own the bounded work wave, tickets own ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone state, and accepted design owns realization decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections.

grounding.quote:
Work-carrier state has one authority chain: Goals own the bounded work wave, the ticket
owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone state, and
accepted design owns realization decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers,
indexes, and generated summaries are projections.

value.label: One-truth work-state projection

conditions: Illustrative recommended document shape
value.definition: The sprint example SPRINT-2026-04-30-operational-projection is active, goal operational-projection-ux, opened and updated 2026-04-30T09:00:00Z. It cites GOALS, PRODUCT and a governing design surface. Its scope is operational projection layout, readability, interaction affordance and visual evidence; it excludes Product truth, data-contract, runtime/governance changes and new constructive carriers. It expects realization_refactor. UXI-001 improves relation-line readability, cites screenshots/2026-04-30/UXI-001.png and carries pending accessibility contrast debt. Closure triggers are timebox, changed surface volume or design-lead request; closure law is a forensic authority walkthrough of each changed state; proof is screenshots and walkthrough notes. Deferred compliance includes screenshots, accessibility and event replay; hidden Product/data-contract drift prevents closure; accepted local debt receives paydown tickets and authority drift is repriced.

View-local concerns include expansion, sort order, filter text, focus and draft input. Product-truth changes include asset writes/creation/moves/deletion; Context, selection authority, pinning or global-state changes; session spawning/attachment/resumption; dispatch of agents, jobs, workorders, graph calls or runtime commands; closure, approval, continuation, lineage, provenance or evidence changes; and publication, acceptance, rejection or supersession of records.

grounding.quote:
UX surfaces are projection and control surfaces. They render admitted truth and
emit typed messages.

order, filter text, focus movement, or draft input.

A UX `Msg` that changes product truth is not merely a UX concern.

value.label: UX surface

value.definition: The Elm Architecture is the adopted constitutional UX process model: State is typed and runtime-held; Msg is the typed algebra of every user/system action; Update is pure (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd), describing rather than performing effects; View is pure State → ViewTree with identical output for identical state; Cmd/Sub describe scheduled effects and subscribed external sources, interpreted by the runtime at the membrane. The runtime loop renders current State, receives Msg, applies Update, interprets resulting Cmds and repeats.

grounding.quote:
- **State** — typed state shape held by the runtime, not by the view
- **Msg** — typed message algebra naming every action a user or system can emit
- **Update** — pure reducer of signature `(Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`; describes side effects as `Cmd` values, does not perform them
- **View** — pure function of signature `State → ViewTree`; given the same state, produces the same output
- **Cmd / Sub** — typed descriptions of side effects to schedule and external sources to subscribe to; interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane

value.label: Elm Architecture

value.definition: The declared effect membrane interprets reducer-produced Cmd values and translates effect outcomes into typed Msg values returned to the reducer. It interprets one declared Cmd per effect and is not a business-continuation controller.

grounding.quote: The membrane interprets `Cmd` values produced by the reducer and translates side-effect outcomes back into `Msg` values delivered to the reducer.

value.label: UX effect membrane

value.definition: Referenced method roles: Spec Method owns constitutional process and lawful re-entry; ODD Method owns graph-native constructive carrier law; Design Module Method owns deterministic module realization. grounding.quote: `UX_METHOD.md` does not duplicate `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`. Where the parent method already governs (immutability, totality, effect-edge discipline, no-semantic-center, coupling), `UX_METHOD.md` cites and extends it. Where UX has concerns the parent does not address (render lifecycle, browser events, layout, accessibility), `UX_METHOD.md` is authoritative.

grounding.quote:
Write an ADR here when the decision:

- governs more than one build tenant under this project
- chooses a concrete realization that satisfies one or more requirements declared under `specification/requirements/` and that requirement applies across tenants
- introduces a structural or interface choice that tenant-local realizations must comply with
- supersedes a prior cross-tenant decision

Write an ADR here when the decision:

- governs only this build tenant (the path segment(s) under `build_tenants/` that identify this tenant — e.g., `<family>/<variant>` or a single-label tenant path)
- chooses a concrete realization that satisfies one or more requirements declared under `specification/requirements/`
- introduces a structural or interface choice future maintainers will need to know about
- supersedes a prior tenant-local decision
